sq.q: Describe Linux capabilities and their significance in process security.
answer: Linux capabilities split root privileges into fine-grained bits assigned per process/thread (permitted, effective, inheritable). Processes can drop unneeded capabilities during execution. Significance: Implements least privilege principle, reducing security risks by limiting process privileges to only what is necessary.

lq.q: Explain Linux capabilities and their role in implementing the principle of least privilege .
answer: Answer Key: Linux capabilities divide root privileges into fine-grained capabilities represented as bitmasks (permitted, effective, inheritable). Processes can drop unneeded capabilities during execution, ensuring they hold only minimal privileges necessary for tasks, directly implementing the principle of least privilege to reduce security risks.
